what_it_does: This paper describes a phase-locked loop (PLL)—a circuit that synchronizes a clock signal to match a reference signal—operating at 13 gigahertz (GHz) with extremely low timing jitter (15.8 femtoseconds RMS, which is 0.0000000000158 seconds) and minimal reference spurs (unwanted frequency components). Using a dual-path architecture, the circuit combines resistive-discharge phase-frequency detection for linearity, a series-resonance voltage-controlled oscillator for noise reduction, and sampling-based filtering.
